wording: Tax year: the calendar year 2026 (Veranlagungszeitraum 2026). A company with a financial year that does not match the calendar year is taxed on the profit of the financial year that ends in 2026 ([§ 7(4) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__7.html)). A German company pays three taxes on its profit: corporate income tax, the solidarity surcharge on that tax, and municipal trade tax. This skill covers the first two in full and summarises the third. For the trade tax method, use `de-trade-tax`.

wording: - **Resident companies (unlimited tax liability).** A company is taxed in Germany on its worldwide income if its place of management (Geschäftsleitung) or its registered seat (Sitz) is in Germany ([§ 1(1) and (2) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__1.html)). This includes the GmbH (and its UG variant), the AG, the SE, the KGaA, cooperatives, other private-law legal persons, and commercial businesses of public bodies. "Place of management" means the centre of top-level management ([§ 10 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__10.html)); the seat is the place named in the articles ([§ 11 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__11.html)). A foreign-registered company run from Germany is therefore fully taxable here.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **Non-resident companies (limited tax liability).** A company with neither its management nor its seat in Germany is taxed only on German-source income ([§ 2 no. 1 KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__2.html)). The main case is a German permanent establishment (Betriebsstätte): any fixed place of business, such as a branch, office, workshop, warehouse, or a building site lasting more than six months ([§ 12 AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__12.html)). A treaty may narrow this.

The law of 14 July 2025 for an immediate tax investment programme (Gesetz für ein steuerliches Investitionssofortprogramm) wrote the cuts into § 23 KStG; the first cut is for 2028. Do not apply 14% or lower to any 2026 or 2027 income.

wording: **Trade tax in one paragraph.** Every GmbH or AG is a trade business in full ([§ 2(2) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__2.html)). Trade income starts from the corporate tax profit, then adds back part of financing costs (interest, rent, leases, royalties above a EUR 200,000 allowance) and makes reductions (for example dividends from holdings of at least 15%). It is rounded down to full EUR 100, multiplied by 3.5%, then by the multiplier of each municipality where the company has an establishment. At a 400% multiplier the trade tax is 14% of trade income, which with 15.825% gives 29.825% in total. Multipliers differ widely by town: always read the client's own notice. A company gets no credit for trade tax against corporate tax (the § 35 EStG credit is for individuals only). Method, add-backs and reductions: see `de-trade-tax`.

wording:
- Interest expense is deductible up to interest income. Net interest above that is deductible only up to 30% of tax EBITDA. After using eligible EBITDA carries from the previous five financial years in chronological order, remaining nondeductible interest is carried forward (Zinsvortrag). Unused current EBITDA capacity is carried into the following five financial years, but no EBITDA carry is generated in a year when interest expense does not exceed interest income or an Absatz 2 escape excludes the barrier (§ 4h(1) sentences 3–6). The statutory chronological rule concerns EBITDA carry vintages; this summary does not supply a complete administrative allocation worksheet for a year mixing old interest carry and current interest.
   - The rule does not apply when net interest is **less than** EUR 3,000,000 (§ 4h(2)(a)). This is a cliff, not an allowance: at EUR 3,000,000 or more, the whole net interest is tested. Absatz 2 does not apply insofar as interest expense is increased by an old interest carry (§ 4h(1) sentence 7); do not exempt that old carry under the current-year escape.

wording: 7. **Share changes ([§ 8c KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__8c.html)).** If more than 50% of the shares or voting rights pass to one buyer (or a group with common interests) within five years, all unused losses so far are lost. Exceptions: transfers inside a 100% group (the group clause), and losses up to the built-in gains (stille Reserven) taxable in Germany. A company that keeps the same business can apply to keep losses under [§ 8d KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__8d.html); the application goes in the return for the year of the transfer.

wording: 8. **Tax group (Organschaft) ([§ 14 KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__14.html), [§ 17 KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__17.html)).** The subsidiary's income is attributed to the parent if: the parent holds the majority of votes without break from the start of the subsidiary's financial year; the subsidiary signs a profit transfer agreement (Gewinnabführungsvertrag) for at least five years and actually carries it out; and the holding belongs to a German PE of the parent. A GmbH subsidiary must also agree to loss assumption by reference to § 302 AktG (§ 17 KStG). For trade tax the subsidiary is treated as a PE of the parent ([§ 2(2) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__2.html)). There is no other form of group relief.

It runs at the earliest from the day the application reaches the BZSt, for at most five years, and cannot be backdated ([BZSt: exemption procedure](https://www.bzst.de/DE/Unternehmen/Kapitalertraege/Kapitalertragsteuerentlastung/Sonderkonstellation/Freistellungsverfahren_50c/freistellungsverfahren_50c_node.html)). Otherwise the shareholder claims a refund from the BZSt under § 50c(3) EStG.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **Foreign corporate recipient within KStG § 2 no. 1:** for a corporation with neither management nor seat in Germany, taxable on its German-source income, two fifths of the 25% withheld and paid over is refunded ([§ 44a(9) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__44a.html)), leaving 15% plus surcharge. This refund is subject to the applicable § 50d(3) anti-abuse test and the § 50c(3) and (5) BZSt refund procedure, including the claim and residence evidence; it is not an automatic entitlement for every foreign entity. Treaty rates may be lower, claimed through the same BZSt procedures.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **Interest.** Withholding under § 43 EStG covers specific types, for example convertible bonds, profit-participating bonds and profit participation rights ([§ 43(1) no. 2 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__43.html)), at 25%. Ordinary loan interest paid to a foreign lender is not in that list, but check the lender's limited tax liability under § 49 EStG before paying gross. Interest between associated EU companies can be relieved under [§ 50g EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__50g.html) (Interest and Royalties Directive).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **Royalties.** Payments to a non-resident for the use of rights or know-how bear 15% withholding ([§ 50a(1) no. 3, (2) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__50a.html)) plus 5.5% surcharge ([§ 3(1) no. 6 SolzG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/solzg_1995/__3.html)). Relief through § 50g EStG, a treaty, or a BZSt exemption certificate. For a limited taxpayer's qualifying § 50a(1) no. 3 remuneration, the payer may omit withholding only to the extent the actual applicable treaty opposes German taxation and this remuneration plus remuneration already received from the same payer by the same recipient in that calendar year does not exceed EUR 10,000. Mere treaty applicability does not establish zero withholding; any remaining German taxing right remains subject to withholding. The payer must still file the withholding return (§ 50c(2) no. 2 and sentence 2 EStG).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **For the non-resident recipient,** corporate tax on income subject to withholding is generally settled by the withholding, unless the income belongs to a German business ([§ 32(1) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__32.html)).
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **CFC rules (Hinzurechnungsbesteuerung).** If German taxpayers control a foreign company, its passive income is added to their German income where it bears tax of less than 15% ([§ 7 AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__7.html), [§ 8(5) AStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/astg/__8.html)). The test compares the foreign tax with 15%, not with the German rate, so the 2028 to 2032 rate cuts do not change it. Refer any CFC case.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: - **Exit tax for companies.** If Germany loses or restricts its right to tax the gain on an asset (for example the asset moves to a foreign PE), the company is treated as selling it at fair market value ([§ 12(1) KStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kstg_1977/__12.html)). For a move to an EU or EEA state the company can apply for a compensating item released over five years ([§ 4g EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__4g.html)). Shareholders who leave Germany: see `leaving-germany-exit-tax`.
